item.title: For California Democrats, single-payer health care is back. Voters have heard it before
item.description: The progressive goal of single-payer health care has become a staple of Democratic platforms, even if it faces as many hurdles as ever.

item.title: California’s new governor must hold down clean energy costs, drive innovation
item.description: In polls voters say they want a cleaner energy future — but not if it wrecks jobs, doubles their bills or pushes out California’s middle class.

item.title: ‘Shocking’: What Supreme Court ruling on transgender policy means for California students
item.description: The court blocked California’s policy barring school districts from requiring teachers to “out” transgender students to their parents, unless the students gave permission.

item.title: Republicans blame Carl DeMaio for party division as his group rakes in millions
item.description: Carl DeMaio, a divisive state lawmaker, continues to upset his colleagues as he works to amass influence through his political organization Reform California — one of the state’s biggest conservative fundraising machines.

item.title: New California law will stop sheriffs from medically examining deaths in their own jails
item.description: Many jail deaths are preventable. To reduce bias and coverups, independent doctors will investigate deaths in custody, starting in 2027.

item.title: How one Cal State campus is trying to break out of a doom loop of declining enrollment
item.description: Several Cal State campuses are caught in a spiral of declining enrollment, threatening their budgets and programs. One in LA is focused on retention and re-enrolling students who dropped out.

item.title: CA schools contend with trans rights, AI and student data privacy
item.description: California’s K-12 schools are grappling with the latest U.S. Supreme Court ruling, a nationwide artificial intelligence contest and personal data violations. Let’s get into it. item.title: Para asistir al baile de graduación o a un partido de fútbol, estudiantes de California tuvieron que entregar sus datos
item.description: La agencia estatal de protección de la privacidad multó a PlayOn con 1.1 millones de dólares por infringir la ley estatal. La empresa, que opera el servicio de venta de entradas GoFan, exigió a estudiantes y padres que compartieran sus datos para acceder a las entradas para eventos de preparatoria.

item.title: Nueva ley de California impedirá que los alguaciles examinen médicamente las muertes en sus propias cárceles
item.description: Muchas muertes en prisión son evitables. Para reducir los sesgos y los encubrimientos, médicos independientes investigarán las muertes bajo custodia a partir de 2027.

item.title: How 9 California Democrats could sabotage their party’s race for governor
item.description: State Democratic party chair Rusty Hicks warned that the nine Democrats currently in the governor’s race could split the primary vote and send two Republicans to the November ballot.
